title: Stormberry Labs link cleaner: provider rules
scope: Tracking parameters, path segments, fragments and redirect wrappers used by the most popular providers (Google, Apple, Meta, Microsoft and LinkedIn, X, TikTok, Snapchat, Reddit, Pinterest, Telegram, Discord, YouTube, Spotify, Netflix, Twitch, SoundCloud, Deezer, Disney+, HBO Max, Amazon, eBay, AliExpress, Temu, Shein, Etsy, Zalando, Booking.com, Airbnb, Wayfair, Nordic shops) plus the analytics, attribution, email and affiliate tools that tag links to them. Merged from three independently verified research groups (G1: Google, Apple, Microsoft and LinkedIn, analytics and attribution; G2: social, messaging and streaming; G3: shops, travel, email and affiliate networks). Every rule names its sources.

matching.host_pattern: A host pattern matches that host and every subdomain of it ("facebook.com" matches www.facebook.com and m.facebook.com). A trailing ".*" stands for any public suffix ("amazon.*" matches amazon.co.uk and amazon.com.br; "google.*" matches www.google.no). Use the Public Suffix List for ".*"; the reference test engine approximates it with one or two alphabetic labels.
matching.pattern_field: hosts[].pattern is an array: the block applies when the URL host matches any of its patterns.
matching.param_names: Compare decoded parameter names case-sensitively. match.type is "exact", "prefix" (the name starts with value) or "regex" (JavaScript syntax, anchored where shown). Percent-decode names before matching, so %24deep_link is $deep_link and __cft__%5B0%5D is __cft__[0].

conditions.paths: apply only when the URL path matches at least one of these regexes
conditions.path_not: never apply when the path matches one of these regexes
conditions.value_regex: apply only when the parameter value matches this regex
conditions.requires_any: apply only when the query also contains one of these parameter names
conditions.url_contains: apply only when the full URL contains one of these strings
conditions.url_not_contains: never apply when the full URL contains one of these strings
conditions.except_hosts: never apply on these hosts (host-pattern rules)

matching.precedence: When several rules match one parameter, the most specific decides: a host rule beats a global rule, and an exact name beats a regex, which beats a prefix. functional_keep entries with effect never_strip win over every rule.

defaults.strip: removed from the suggested clean link and shown in red
defaults.ask: shown in red but kept in the suggested clean link until the user decides
defaults.keep: functional: shown as needed, never removed

matching.merge_rule: Where the verified groups disagreed on the default, the most conservative value won (keep, then ask, then strip), except for affiliate parameters, which follow affiliate_policy.
matching.order: Unwrap offline redirects first (repeat up to five times, cleaning each destination), then strip path segments, then query parameters, then key=value pairs in the fragment. Keep the order and the original encoding of every parameter that stays, and drop an empty ? or #.

affiliate_policy.rule: Every parameter with an "affiliate" field pays the person or site that shared the link. It is stripped by default and shown in red with the label "pays the sharer"; the app offers one switch, "Keep the sharer's affiliate credit", which keeps every affiliate parameter of that network together (for example Amazon tag, or eBay campid with mkevt, mkcid, mkrid, toolid and customid). Setting default to "ask" keeps them in the suggested clean link until the user decides.
affiliate_policy.why: The verifiers disagreed: two groups marked Amazon tag, Apple at, Rakuten ranMID and ranEAID, and Telegram ref as "ask", while the shop group stripped every affiliate parameter and asked the app to explain the commission loss. ClearURLs, uBlock Origin, AdGuard and DandelionSprout strip them by default; Firefox Strip on Share deliberately keeps Amazon tag, and DandelionSprout ships an opt-in affiliate allow-list. Keeping one parameter of a network while stripping the rest rarely preserves the credit (Rakuten needs ranSiteID, eBay needs the mk* set), so the decision is made per network.

functional_keep.note: Strip only listed names (a deny-list), never every unknown parameter; unlisted ones such as Instagram img_index or SoundCloud in= are unverified and must survive. Never strip path segments except the Amazon-style /ref= segment. Compare parameter names case-sensitively (Facebook source is ask, Source and Medium are strip; Bing lists both PC and pc).
functional_keep.basis: Design rule of the merged table (verified in G2); it adds no parameter, so it needs no external source.

functional_keep.note: Generic names that are tracking only on one host or under one condition and functional elsewhere: source, from, src, origin, cid, eid, pid, c, campaign, creative, adgroup, referrer, ei, ref, channel, content, medium, device, ch, ut, PID, scid, sv1, lid, email, campaignId. Never strip them globally; apply them only within the scope given. Awin documents source=aw as its channel marker, but source is functional on many sites, so it is kept.

Not stripped because no checked list or platform document names them, so they are kept until a source appears: ghc, lq and originalSubdomain; Shein src_identifier, Etsy ls, Wayfair piid, FINN finnMail and ci.

Google Search: q (query), tbm and udm (search type or mode), start (results page), tbs (filters), hl and gl (language and country), safe and num. Unfurl documents q, start, tbm and udm; DandelionSprout warns that prmd and stick must not be removed, strips udm only when it is empty, and removes num only when it has two or more digits (issue 1186).
google.<TLD>/url (url, q), googleadservices.com/pagead/aclk (adurl) and search.app (link) hold the destination: unwrap them, never strip them.
Google Maps: every path segment (/place/<name>/@lat,lng,zoom/data=!...) and the Maps URLs API parameters.

Google Play: id (the app) and hl on /store/apps/details; q and c (c=apps) on /store/search, where removing c caused a redirect loop (DandelionSprout issue 475). Cleaners strip only pcampaignid and referrer on Play.
Google News: hl, gl and ceid choose the edition and language; ClearURLs exempts news.google.com URLs that carry hl.
*.translate.goog: _x_tr_sl, _x_tr_tl and _x_tr_hl set the translation languages; only _x_tr_pto is stripped.
ClearURLs exempts accounts.google.com and myaccount.google.com (including Google OAuth paths) from its Google rules and from its global rules; treat them as no-touch.
ClearURLs exempts docs.google.com, mail.google.com/mail/u/ and Drive from its Google rules; treat them as no-touch for Google host rules.
apps.apple.com: the app ID in the path (/id123456789) is the link; the slug and region segment (/gb/) are functional, and app=messages opens the App Store for iMessage page.

music.apple.com ?i= (the song within an album) and podcasts.apple.com ?i= (the episode) MUST stay, together with the numeric album, app or umc ID in the path. Tidy URL strips i on music.apple.com, which breaks song links; do not copy that rule.
Apple affiliate links: at (affiliate token) and app=music go together; Apple asks for app=music on Apple Music affiliate links. If the user keeps the affiliate's credit, keep both.
Bing: q, first (results offset), setlang, filters, rdr and rdrig; DandelionSprout notes that removing filters, rdr or rdrig breaks Bing, and Tidy URL allow-lists q, tsc, iss, id, view and setlang.
Outlook Safe Links: url holds the destination (unwrap it); data and sdata are never needed once unwrapped, and data carries the recipient's email address.

LinkedIn path IDs are the link: /jobs/view/<id>, /in/<slug>, /posts/<slug>-activity-<id>-<suffix>, /feed/update/urn:li:activity:<id>. Brave removes only named tracking parameters on these paths and leaves the path alone.
otpToken: Tidy URL allow-lists it, labelling it a one-time password token; show it as personal rather than strip it silently (it is "ask").

app.adjust.com: redirect, redirect_ios, redirect_android, redirect_macos, redirect_windows, redirect_windows-phone, fallback and deep_link hold destinations; unwrap redirect or fallback rather than strip.
*.onelink.me: af_r (all platforms) and af_web_dp (desktop) hold destinations.
*.app.link: $fallback_url and country variants such as $fallback_url_de hold destinations.
Marketo mkt_tok on unsubscribe and email web-view URLs is needed for the page to work: the mkt_tok rule never applies when the URL contains unsubscribe, emailWebview or mkt_unsubscribe.

YouTube: keep v, t (seconds or 1m30s), list, index, start, end, playlist, loop and lc (comment highlight; LUS deliberately disabled its lc rule); keep the path IDs /watch, /shorts/<id>, /live/<id> and youtu.be/<id>.

X / Twitter: keep the path /<user>/status/<id> (plus /photo/N, /video/N) and q and f on /search; t is a tracker only on /status/ paths and must stay elsewhere, for example on x.com/i/redirect?url= (uBO note; Brave excludes /i/redirect).

Facebook: keep v (watch), story_fbid and id (story.php), fbid (photo), comment_id and reply_comment_id (verified on 2026-10-10: no consulted list strips them on Facebook); set and lower-case source are ask; eav is ask because removal breaks downloads (LUS).
ClearURLs exempts photo.php, /photo/download/, /dialog/share, /dialog/send and plugins/ajax paths on Facebook.
Messenger: keep ref on m.me links; it is the documented way a business receives context (delivered in messaging_postbacks or messaging_referrals webhooks).
Instagram and Threads: keep /p/<code>/, /reel/<code>/, /stories/<user>/<id>/ and threads.com/@<user>/post/<code>.
functional_keep.basis: Observed URL formats; no consulted list strips path segments on these sites, so keeping the path is the default.

functional_keep.note: WhatsApp: keep wa.me/<number> and text, api.whatsapp.com/send phone and text, chat.whatsapp.com/<invite> and whatsapp.com/channel/<id>. wa.me/<number> carries a phone number: functional, but worth flagging to the user as personal data.

Telegram: keep start (bot payload), startgroup, startchannel, admin, single, thread, comment, t (media timestamp), and url and text on t.me/share; ref on bot links is an affiliate referral (see the ref rule).

Discord: keep invite codes (discord.gg/<code>, discord.com/invite/<code>) and message paths discord.com/channels/<guild>/<channel>/<message>. Discord adds no tracking wrapper; only the generic source, campaign, medium and ref tags are stripped (Tidy URL, LUS).

Mastodon: no tracking parameters or link wrappers expected, re-verified on 2026-10-10: zero Mastodon entries in ClearURLs, Brave, Firefox, uBO, AdGuard, LUS, Tidy URL or Neat URL, and Mastodon's TextFormatter renders the original URL as href with rel=nofollow noopener, no redirect.
Snapchat: keep /add/<user>, story.snapchat.com/p/<uuid>/<id> and locale; timestamp is stripped only when its value is 0.
Reddit: keep /r/<sub>/comments/<id>/<slug>/<comment_id>/ and context (number of parent comments shown); no list strips it.
TikTok: keep /@<user>/video/<id>, /@<user>/photo/<id>, lang (Tidy URL allow-list) and q on /search. Do not copy Firefox's TikTok list verbatim: it strips q and t on every path.
Pinterest: keep /pin/<id>/.
functional_keep.basis: Observed URL format; no consulted list strips path segments on Pinterest.

functional_keep.note: Spotify: keep the path ID (/track, /album, /playlist, /episode, /show, /artist, optional /intl-xx/ prefix), t on episodes (timestamp sharing), uri (LUS: "Don't remove uri, as it seems to involve source songs"), nd and go (Tidy URL allow-list).
Netflix: keep /title/<id>, /watch/<id> and jbv on /browse (the title ID; it can be rewritten to /title/<id>).
Twitch: keep the channel path, /videos/<id>, t on VODs (for example t=05h19m48s), clips.twitch.tv/<slug> and device-code on /activate.
SoundCloud: keep /<artist>/<track> and the #t= time fragment from Share at a time. The help page returned 403 to the verifier on 2026-10-10 and was not re-confirmed.
Deezer: keep /<lang>/track|album|playlist|artist/<id>; host, origin, deferredFl and utm_* are trackers.

Tidal: keep /browse/track/<id> and the /u path suffix (a universal link that lets the recipient pick another service). The source now returns 404 and the /u wording was confirmed only through the search index on 2026-10-10; keeping it is the safe default anyway. No Tidal tracking parameters are in any consulted list.
Amazon Music: keep /albums/<ASIN>, /tracks/<ASIN>, /artists/<ASIN> and trackAsin (no consulted list strips trackAsin).
Prime Video: keep /detail/<id>/, /dp/<ASIN> and amazon.*/gp/video/detail/<ASIN>.

Disney+ and HBO Max: keep the path IDs (/movies/<slug>/<id>, /series/<slug>/<id>, /video/<id>, play.hbomax.com/<type>/<id>); only the listed campaign tags are stripped. For HBO Max / Max, only hbomax.com source (LUS) and the trk.hbomax.com wrapper (Tidy URL) are in any list; nothing was found for max.com.

Amazon: /dp/<ASIN> (10 characters) is the product, with /gp/product/<ASIN> and /gp/aw/d/<ASIN> as equivalents; the SEO slug before /dp/ is optional text. psc (selected variation) and smid (seller) must stay: removing psc breaks size selection and removing smid switches to the default seller.

Amazon search pages /s: k (query), s (sort; uBO and AdGuard note removing it breaks sorting), m (seller filter; DandelionSprout disabled removal), rh (DandelionSprout: bad idea to remove), and keywords, rnid and refinements (ClearURLs exempts /s?).

Amazon: ie on redirect endpoints (/b/ref=..., /sspa/click) and every parameter of /sspa/click and /gp/slredirect/picassoRedirect.html stay; unwrap picassoRedirect instead and leave /sspa/click opaque.

eBay: the numeric item ID in /itm/<id> (an optional slug may precede it) is the link; var (variation) must stay (AdGuard issue 208605); iid is kept by DandelionSprout after a breakage report; epid is ask (Tidy URL keeps it).

eBay search /sch/i.html: _nkw (query), _sacat (category; DandelionSprout exempts eBay), _pgn (page), rt and _blrs (DandelionSprout notes removal breaks filter buttons or search confirmation), and the LH_* filters.
AliExpress: /item/<id>.html is the product; sku_id and pdp_ext_f carry the chosen variant (the Tidy URL allow-list keeps both).
Temu: the goods ID sits in the path ("...-g-<goods_id>.html"); keep the path (format observed, not documented).
functional_keep.basis: Observed URL format, not documented by Temu; no consulted list strips the path.

functional_keep.note: Etsy: keep /listing/<listing id>/<slug> and /shop/<name>.

Booking.com: keep /hotel/<cc>/<name>.html plus checkin, checkout, group_adults, group_children, no_rooms, dest_id and all_sr_blocks (stay dates, party and room selection); no source lists these as trackers.
Airbnb: keep /rooms/<id>; stay dates and guest counts are not listed as trackers by any source (ClearURLs removes only federated_search_id, search_type, source and source_impression_id).
Wayfair: keep the /pdp/ path; only the listed email and campaign parameters are removed.
FINN: keep the item path (/recommerce/forsale/item/<id>); only alertType, stored-id and nocache are removed.

path_rules.name: /ref=<code> (path segment)
path_rules.provider: Amazon internal referral code in the path
path_rules.reveals: Which list, search-result position or widget produced the link (for example /ref=sr_1_6, or /ref=nosim on affiliate links).

breakage.detail: none: the product still resolves from /dp/<ASIN>

path_rules.note: Applies on every amazon.* page (shop, Amazon Music, amazon.*/gp/video) and on primevideo.com. ClearURLs rawRule \/ref=[^/?]* and Tidy URL replace (\/ref|&ref_)=[^\/?]*.

A session-like segment after /ref= (for example /ref=pd_sbs_14_1/262-3877129-1714269 in a DandelionSprout example) is not removed by any list, because the ClearURLs rawRule stops at the next slash; the safest fix is a canonical rebuild to https://www.amazon.<tld>/dp/<ASIN>, keeping only psc and smid. Offer it, do not apply it silently.
https://www.google.<TLD>/amp/s/<host>/<path> is Google's AMP viewer; the real URL is https://<host>/<path>. Offline.
https://<x>.cdn.ampproject.org/c/s/<host>/<path> is the AMP cache; the real URL is https://<host>/<path>. Offline.
https://<x>.turbopages.org/<host>/s/<path> is Yandex Turbo; the real URL is https://<host>/<path>. Offline.

www.twitch.tv/r/e/<base64-json>/... is a path-embedded email tracker. The base64 decodes to JSON, but a destination can be rebuilt only when the JSON has name=twitch_favorite_up (a go-live email), as https://www.twitch.tv/<channel>; other email types are opaque.
click.redditmail.com/CL0/<url-encoded destination>/...: the destination is the first path segment; unwrap with ^/CL0/([^/]+)/ and percent-decode.
amazon-adsystem.com/x/c/<token>/<destination>: the destination is embedded in the path.
prf.hn/click/camref:<id>/pubref:<x>/ar:<y>/destination:<url>: the affiliate IDs and the destination are path segments.
Amazon SES awstrack.me/L0/<url-encoded destination>/... and Postmark click.pstmrk.it/2s/<destination>/...: the destination is in the path (see also postmark-https and postmark-http).

Reddit /r/<sub>/s/<code> share links carry an opaque share code whose value changes every time a link is generated; only Reddit can expand it. Show it red as "Reddit share link, cannot be cleaned offline".
tiktok.com/t/<code> and vm.tiktok.com/<code> are short share codes that do not contain the video ID; resolving them needs a redirect, so they cannot be cleaned offline.

Never touch these paths: Google Maps /maps/place/<name>/@<lat>,<lng>,<zoom>/data=!..., Amazon /dp/<ASIN>, eBay /itm/<id>, AliExpress /item/<id>.html, Etsy /listing/<id>, Booking /hotel/<cc>/<name>.html, and the Tidal /u suffix (a universal chooser page).

When the fragment is a list of key=value pairs, apply the same parameter rules inside it and drop an empty #. ClearURLs already applies its parameter rules inside the fragment (so utm_* after # is removable); DandelionSprout says uBlock Origin and AdGuard cannot remove anything after #, so an app should do it itself. Skip text fragments (#:~:text=) and route-style fragments that start with / or !.
Matomo reads campaign fields from the fragment as well as the query (#pk_campaign=..., #pk_kwd=..., #mtm_campaign=...); strip those keys inside the fragment and drop an empty #.

The Google tag linker _gl can be placed after # (https://example.com#_gl=1~abcde5~) when the site sets url_position to fragment; strip it there too and drop an empty #. Google appends gad_* before any fragment, so those are query parameters.

#:~:text=<passage> text fragments scroll a page to a quoted passage; Google scrolls featured-snippet clicks to the quoted section automatically. They reveal the passage, not the person: keep, optionally ask.
Google Images #imgrc=<id> opens the chosen image; DandelionSprout keeps fir and usg when #imgrc is present.
SoundCloud #t=<time> (from Share at a time) is functional: keep it.

redirects.label: Facebook link shim (l.facebook.com, lm.facebook.com)
redirects.note: ClearURLs matches l plus at most one more letter (lm.facebook.com).

redirects.label: Instagram link shim (l.instagram.com)
redirects.note: ClearURLs: instagram redirection .*u=.

redirects.label: WhatsApp click-to-chat link wrapper (l.wl.co)
redirects.note: Hosted on Facebook infrastructure; lower confidence, single source.

redirects.label: Facebook share link (/share/<type>/<code>/)
redirects.note: New-style share links from the app's Copy link; the code is resolved by Facebook.

redirects.label: X redirect (/i/redirect)
redirects.note: Brave excludes /i/redirect from stripping; t must never be stripped here in place, but unwrapping discards it with the wrapper.

redirects.label: X link shortener (t.co)
redirects.note: X wraps every posted link; its link service measures how many times a link is clicked.

redirects.label: TikTok share short links (vm.tiktok.com, tiktok.com/t/)
redirects.note: The short code does not contain the video ID; resolving it needs a redirect.

redirects.label: YouTube attribution link
redirects.note: u is a path: prefix https://www.youtube.com to the decoded value.

redirects.label: Reddit email click wrapper (click.redditmail.com/CL0/, path wrapper)
redirects.note: The destination is the first path segment after /CL0/, percent-encoded; ClearURLs also handles an older ?url= form.

redirects.label: Reddit post shortener (redd.it)
redirects.note: Plain post shortener with no tracking; expansion to the full post URL is optional.

redirects.label: Reddit share link (/r/<sub>/s/<code>)
redirects.note: Opaque share code whose value changes every time a link is generated; only Reddit can expand it. Show it red as "Reddit share link, cannot be cleaned offline".

redirects.label: Pinterest short link (pin.it)
redirects.note: Pinterest's official shortener; redirects to pinterest.com.

redirects.label: Spotify short link (spotify.link)
redirects.note: Short link, not a plain 301; resolved client-side.

redirects.label: Deezer share link (link.deezer.com/s/)
redirects.note: deezer.page.link and dzr.page.link were dropped by the verifier: no source confirms them.

redirects.label: Twitch email tracking wrapper (/r/e/<base64-json>/, path wrapper)
redirects.note: The base64 segment decodes to JSON; only when name is twitch_favorite_up (a go-live email) can a destination be rebuilt, as https://www.twitch.tv/<channel>. Other email types are opaque.

redirects.label: Telegram share intent (t.me/share)
redirects.note: A share intent, not a tracker: show the embedded URL rather than silently replacing the link.

redirects.label: Amazon short links (amzn.to, amzn.eu/d, amzn.asia, a.co, amzn.com)
redirects.note: Cannot be expanded offline; flag as "opens a redirect, contents unknown".

redirects.label: Amazon sponsored-product redirect (picassoRedirect.html)
redirects.note: url is a relative path: prefix the same Amazon host, then clean.

redirects.label: Amazon sponsored-product click (/sspa/click)
redirects.note: Do not strip its parameters; no source documents the destination parameter, so treat it as opaque.

redirects.label: Amazon ad redirect (amazon-adsystem.com/x/c/, path wrapper)
redirects.note: The destination is embedded in the path.

redirects.label: AliExpress affiliate links (s.click.aliexpress.com)
redirects.note: /e/<code> is an affiliate short link; on deep_link.htm leave aff_short_key alone (uBO exempts it because it is the redirect itself).

redirects.label: Awin click redirect (awin1.com)
redirects.note: ued on cread.php; p on cread.php and awclick.php.

redirects.label: CJ Affiliate click redirect
redirects.note: Without url= the destination is not in the URL.

redirects.label: Rakuten Advertising redirect (click.linksynergy.com)
redirects.note: ClearURLs and tidy-url accept any linksynergy path carrying murl=.

redirects.label: impact.com partner links
redirects.note: microsoft.msafflnk.net is listed separately under Microsoft.

redirects.label: Partnerize click link (prf.hn, path wrapper)
redirects.note: Affiliate IDs (camref, pubref, ar) and the destination are path segments.

redirects.label: ShareASale click redirect
redirects.note: urllink has no scheme: prepend https://.

redirects.label: Mailchimp campaign click tracker (list-manage.com)
redirects.note: The destination is held on Mailchimp's servers; warn the user.

redirects.label: Amazon SES click wrapper (awstrack.me, path wrapper)
Postmark click wrapper (click.pstmrk.it, path wrapper)
redirects.note: 2s, 2sm, 2ts, 3s and 3ts variants: prepend https://.

redirects.label: Postmark click wrapper, plain-http variants
redirects.note: 2, 2m and 3 variants: prepend http://.

redirects.label: ActiveCampaign link tracker
redirects.note: redirectUrl is base64.

redirects.label: GovDelivery click tracker
redirects.note: The https URL is embedded in the tracking URL.

redirects.label: Other email click-tracking redirects
redirects.note: Click trackers from senders such as Iterable, Brevo, HubSpot, Klaviyo or Salesforce Marketing Cloud hold the destination on the sender's servers, as Mailchimp documents for its own; no open list unwraps them, so treat them as opaque.
